title: First Year Seminar for Business Pre-Majors
description: Provides opportunities for students to interact with faculty and staff in a small seminar setting. Students develop learning strategies, time management, and interpersonal skills, and are introduced to various campus resources (e.g., library, advising, career, health and wellness services, etc.).

title: Fowler Scholars Seminar I
description: Understanding, applying and critiquing ethical business theories as well as examining personal branding and corresponding narrative.
notes: Not open to students with four units of credit in GEN S 200. Maximum four units of GEN S 200 and B A 210.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Ethical Decision Making in Business
description: Theoretical concepts and dimensions of ethics in business decisions. Ethics of decision alternatives using different approaches and philosophies, with application of an integrative ethical decision model to cases from various business subdisciplines.

title: Career and Professional Readiness
description: Preparation for transition from academic life to professional career. Emphasis on career readiness skills of self-awareness, professional etiquette, personal branding, networking, and job search techniques.

title: Foundations of Business in a Global Environment
description: Introduction to the program of study leading to the Bachelor of Science in Business Administration. Integration of various business disciplines to accomplish strategic goals. Presentation of the concept of global awareness, one of the fundamental pillars of global competency necessary in today’s business world.

title: Lavin Entrepreneur I Seminar
description: Lavin entrepreneurs will be introduced to entrepreneurship as a potential path for future career development. Students will begin developing entrepreneurial competencies, professional networks, and be introduced to the basics of ideation, opportunity recognition, and business model development.

title: Lavin Entrepreneur II Seminar
description: Lavin entrepreneurs will continue building their entrepreneurial competencies and mindset, utilizing entrepreneurship frameworks for business opportunity assessment, ideation, and feasibility analysis techniques in ventures, and how to interact and negotiate with strategic partners.

title: Fundamentals of Finance
description: Objectives of financial management. Financing the business enterprise. Internal financial management. Introduction to the cost of capital, valuation, dividend policy, leverage, international finance, and the techniques of present value and its applications. Sources of capital.

title: Management and Organizational Behavior
description: Human behavior at individual, interpersonal, and group levels including effect of organization structure on behavior. Emphasis on managerial roles, historical evolution of management, ethics, and behavior in multicultural contexts.

title: Introduction to Operations and Supply Chain Management
description: Managerial concepts and quantitative methods associated with the design, execution, and management of operations and supply chain systems.

title: Marketing
description: Function of marketing in organizations and society. Strategic marketing planning in domestic and global settings to include marketing concepts, consumer behavior, market research, product planning, pricing, distribution, promotion, and influence of the external environment on marketing decisions.

title: Business Honors Seminar
description: Current issues affecting local, national, and global business environments.

title: Business Internship
description: Internships with business firms, non-profit organizations, or government agencies. Work done under joint supervision of intern organization and academic supervisor.
notes: Not applicable for credit in the major.

title: Small Business Consulting
description: Counseling of existing small businesses. Application of principles from all fields of business administration.

title: Fowler Scholars Seminar II
description: Understanding, applying and critiquing ethical business theories as well as examining personal branding and corresponding narrative. Leading both project teams and guest speaker topics.
notes: Not open to students with six units of credit in GEN S 400. Maximum six units of GEN S 400 and B A 410.

title: Lavin Entrepreneur III Seminar
description: Lavin entrepreneurs will focus on implementing learned entrepreneurial competencies into refined business models, refining start-up opportunities through customer iteration and development. Understand data metrics, successful customer interaction, and pivoting the business model toward success.

title: Lavin Entrepreneur IV Seminar
description: The final deliverable of this capstone course in presenting an iterated business model canvas to potential investors. Lavin entrepreneurs have the potential, knowledge, and tools to launch a company, bring their viable business opportunity to life.

title: Selected Topics in Business Administration
description: Selected areas of concern in business administration.

title: Investigation and Report
description: A comprehensive and original study of a problem connected with business administration under the direction of one or more members of the Fowler College of Business staff.

title: Contemporary Executive Toolkit
description: Study of aspects of an executive’s work. Include frameworks, skills, and practices to improve effectiveness. Topics include managing oneself, building executive presence, balancing demands and time, managing difficult conversations, and demonstrating your uniqueness.

title: Business Economics
description: Microeconomic and macroeconomic environments of business. Assessing and forecasting the impact of market structure, economic climate, and governmental policies on pricing, operations, and competitive strategy.
notes: Not open to students with credit in Business Administration 653.

title: Marketing
description: Role and function of marketing in the organization and society. Planning, implementation, and evaluation of marketing strategies and programs.
notes: Not open to students with credit in

title: Operations and Supply Chain Management
description: Managerial concepts and quantitative methods associated with the design, execution, and management of operations and supply chain systems.

title: Financial Reporting and Analysis
description: Financial accounting in profit-directed organizations. Concepts, frameworks, terminology, and tools used to understand and analyze the financial consequences of business activities.
notes: Not open to students with credit in Business Administration 625.

title: Business Ethics and Corporate Responsibility
description: Decision-making strategies; principles, rules, and values that ground ethical behavior in the world of business.

title: Statistical Analysis
description: Applications of statistics for problem solving and managerial decision-making.

title: Managerial Economics
description: Microeconomic environments of business. Assessing and forecasting impacts of economic climate, governmental policy, and of market structure on competitive strategy, operations, and pricing.

title: Operations and Supply Chain Management
description: Managerial concepts and quantitative methods associated with the design, execution, and management of operations and supply chain systems.

title: Marketing
description: Foundational concepts and development of marketing strategies and plans.

title: Business Analytics
description: Business analytics techniques for predictive modeling and customer segmentation. Applications include churn management, business experiments, cluster segmentation, and market basket analysis.

title: Managerial Accounting
description: Budgeting, cost control, job costing, overhead allocation, and reporting.

title: Legal Environment of Business
description: Sources of law. Procedures and ethics associated with implementation of law. Law of torts and intellectual property. Agency and employment, business organizations, contracts and sales, negotiable instruments and banking.

title: Managerial Marketing
description: Identification, understanding, and resolution of marketing issues in organizations. Theoretical and quantitative tools within a decision-making framework to inform organizational strategic directions.

title: Organizational Behavior and Leadership
description: Study of individuals and groups within an organizational context. Topics include leadership, individual differences, organizational design, group processes and characteristics, organizational processes and practices; and influence of these on individual, group, and organizational effectiveness.

title: Financial Management
description: Explore role of finance in a shareholder value based framework. Financial analysis and planning, investment, capital structure, financial markets, capital raising and capital disbursement decisions, valuation, and corporate restructuring.
notes: Not open to students with credit in Business Administration 665.

title: Strategic Thinking
description: How top managers should formulate and implement strategy across organizational levels and functions by thinking in a logical, holistic, and integrated manner.

title: Seminar in Contemporary Challenges
description: Challenges facing managers of organizations in modern society: organizational, human resources, operational, economic, environmental, political, international, and technological issues.

title: Field Studies in Business
description: Application of business concepts to real world organizations. Students work under supervision of a faculty member to perform a project utilizing theories and principles from previous business coursework.

title: International Business Development Practicum
description: Strategic analysis of business opportunities. Problem definition, data collection, analysis, and prioritization of solution mechanisms. Preparation for comprehensive examination.

title: Business Consulting
description: Strategic analysis of business problems in a consulting or simulation context. Problem definition analysis and prioritization of solution mechanisms. Culminating experience for students in the M.B.A. program under Plan B.

title: Integrative Business Analysis
description: Integrative business analysis through cases and simulations. Preparation for the comprehensive examination for students in the M.B.A. program (Plan B).

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Thesis
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis is granted final approval.

title: Comprehensive Examination Extension
description: Registration required of students whose only requirement is completion of the comprehensive examination for the master’s degree. Registration in 799C limited to two semesters.
